title: Personalized adaptive thresholds for arrhythmia detectors in long-term ECG monitoring

record.title: Personalized adaptive thresholds for arrhythmia detectors in long-term ECG monitoring
record.abstract: Fixed detection thresholds in ambulatory arrhythmia monitors fail to account for inter-individual variability in cardiac electrophysiology and body habitus, leading to systematically elevated false-positive rates in certain patient subgroups. This paper proposes a patient-adaptive threshold framework for wearable ECG arrhythmia detectors in which detection parameters are continuously updated using an online Bayesian update rule applied to a rolling window of high-confidence rhythm annotations from the preceding monitoring period. The method requires no pre-training on patient-specific data and is therefore directly applicable from the first hour of monitoring. Computational overhead is bounded to allow deployment alongside an existing QRS detector on an ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller. The framework is evaluated on long-term recordings from 58 patients with documented paroxysmal AF. Compared with fixed-threshold detectors, the adaptive approach reduces the per-patient median false-alarm rate by 47% while maintaining sensitivity above 91% across all subgroups stratified by age, sex, and body mass index. The results support patient-adaptive personalization as a practical and computationally tractable strategy for improving specificity in clinical-grade wearable cardiac monitors.
